CMPE 257 · San José State University

Early Prediction of Reading Performance

Reproducing Shangguan et al., NeurIPS 2024, on the ECRI first-grade dataset: from 16 start-of-year measures, predict which children will make above-average reading growth by spring.

Predict a student Models Paper vs ours

Can we spot slow reading growth in the fall?

Teachers need to know early which first graders will fall behind. We train models on what is known at the start of the year and test them on schools they have never seen.

16 fall features8 reading tests, 3 about the student, 5 about the classroom
→
Modellinear, tree, ensemble, neural network
→
Progress labelhigh growth if the spring gain beats the control group's average gain
→
Test on new schools5-fold cross-validation grouped by school

Model results same 706 students, same school folds

Mean over 5 school-grouped folds. Neural networks: mean over 3 seeds × 5 folds on the same 706 students.

Predict a student

Enter a first grader's fall test scores. Each model predicts whether the student will perform better by spring, meaning their score grows more than the average student's in the control group.

What each model predicts best model first

ECRI dataset

Enhanced Core Reading Instruction study: first graders tested in the fall and again in the spring. Classrooms were assigned to the ECRI reading intervention or to a control group.

Students6,916first graders
Schools44groups for CV
Teachers171classrooms
Features16all from the fall
Targets2Word ID, Word Attack

Who can be used

6,916all students · MaskMLP pretraining only (no labels needed)
946have the spring outcome, so a label
936all 8 reading tests · paper's rule, neural models
706all 16 features · traditional models

How the label is made

Gain
spring raw score − fall raw score (Woodcock test)
Bar
average gain of the control group (no intervention): 26.32 Word ID, 10.75 Word Attack
Label
high growth if the student's gain is above the bar, otherwise low growth
Balance
Word ID 54% high (383 of 706) · Word Attack 59% high (416 of 706)
Testing
5-fold GroupKFold by school (main) and by student; tuning uses an inner 4-fold split of the training schools only
